title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: within the notes on Gauss–Manin connections, Picard–Fuchs equations and Cartier's operation, this page gives a sheaf-theoretic, axiomatic characterisation of the Schwarzian derivative. Its purpose is to set up the torsor of projective structures on a curve, which the next page goes on to construct.

(I) Setting. Let X be a smooth complex analytic curve.
- E_X is the sheaf of étale (locally biholomorphic, f' ≠ 0) maps from opens of X to the affine line A^1(C).
- P_X is the analogous sheaf of étale maps to P^1(C).

Theorem. There is a morphism of sheaves of sets G : E_X × E_X → ω_X^{⊗2} (quadratic differentials) with the following properties.
- (a) G is a possibly nonlinear differential operator. In a local coordinate t, G(f,g) = R(f,…,f^{(n)}; g,…,g^{(n)}) dt², where R = P/Q is rational with holomorphic coefficients. Q does not vanish identically on étale f,g, and the only poles occur where f' or g' vanish. A bracketed conjecture says that, with P and Q coprime, Q = f'^p g'^q.
- (b) Cocycle condition: G(f,g) + G(g,h) = G(f,h).
- (c) Invariance under the generators of PGL_2 acting on the second argument: g ↦ ag (a ∈ C*), g ↦ g + b, and g ↦ 1/g when g has no zeros.
- (d) Rigidity: if G(f,g) = 0 and f, g have the same 2-jet at some point of a connected U, then f = g.
- Uniqueness for fixed X: any two such G are related by G' = φG with φ ∈ Γ(X, O_X^*).

(II) If X is allowed to vary, with G required to be compatible with étale morphisms X' → X, the indeterminacy drops to G' = cG with c ∈ C*.

Marginal NB.
- (a) G extends to P_X × P_X (by Möbius invariance).
- (c) For fixed f, the map g ↦ G(f,g) is a differential operator.

Identification of G. By the next page, G(f,g) = C(f,g) = [(-2g'''/g' + 3(g''/g')²) - (same for f)] dt², which is -2(S(g) - S(f)) dt², where S is the classical Schwarzian.
- G is a coboundary c(g) - c(f), with c taking values in a canonical ω^{⊗2}-torsor T_X.
- The induced map PGL_2\P_X → T_X is an isomorphism, so projective structures form a torsor under quadratic differentials.
- Section III (next page) passes to smooth relative curves over arbitrary schemes, using Hasse–Schmidt derivatives D^{(k)}. The normalised operator C/12 = -S/6 is defined over Z and unique up to sign ±1.

Why uniqueness is plausible.
- Möbius-invariant differential functions of g are functions of t, S(g), S(g)', … .
- Write c(g) = Ψ(t, S(g), S(g)', …). Condition (d) forces the equation Ψ(s) = Ψ(s0) to have only the solution s = s0 for arbitrary holomorphic s0 (any holomorphic function is S of some g with a prescribed 2-jet).
- If Ψ involves derivatives of s, this ODE has nontrivial local solutions, so Ψ must be of order 0.
- An injective rational function of s with no extra poles is affine in s, giving φS + const.
- Requiring compatibility with all étale maps then forces φ to be a constant.
errors: 'R est une fonction rationnelle en 2n variables': the arguments f,…,f^{(n)}, g,…,g^{(n)} are 2n+2 variables (slip).

The uniqueness statement 'G' = φG' is asserted without proof. Its truth rests essentially on (d) and on the no-extra-poles condition in (a): without them, e.g. G = (S(g)-S(f)) + (S(g)-S(f))' would satisfy (b) and (c). The argument sketched in the reconstruction appears to close this gap, but it is not on the page.
The claim Q = f'^p g'^q is explicitly conjectural ('On doit pouvoir montrer'); it is plausible and true for the Schwarzian, but unproved here.
Minor: (d) needs the 2-jets of f and g to agree at the point (order 2 contact), which is exactly what fixes a Möbius transformation; the wording 'coïncident à l'ordre 2' is correct but terse.

ideas.what: Axiomatic characterisation of the Schwarzian (up to a unit) as the unique differential-operator cocycle E_X × E_X → ω^{⊗2} that is PGL_2-invariant and rigid on 2-jets
ideas.modern_name: Schwarzian derivative as the unique PGL_2-invariant 1-cocycle / projective connection
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Schwarz, Cayley); cocycle and uniqueness viewpoint in Kirillov, Ovsienko–Tabachnikov, Gelfand–Fuks cohomology H^1(Vect, F_2)

ideas.what: Passing from fixed X (indeterminacy O_X^*) to X varying over étale morphisms (indeterminacy C*): uniqueness as a natural transformation on the étale site of curves
ideas.modern_name: Natural (functorial) differential operators on the site of curves with étale maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Natural-operators tradition (Kolář–Michor–Slovák), not specifically for this case

ideas.what: Extension of G to étale maps into P^1 (margin NB a), preparing the identification of PGL_2\P_X with a torsor under ω^{⊗2}
ideas.modern_name: Sheaf of projective structures as an ω^{⊗2}-torsor (sl_2-opers)

ideas.what: Rationality and pole-structure condition on the operator (denominator only powers of f', g')
ideas.modern_name: Differential invariants of PGL_2 on jets of étale maps

missed.claim: A clean sheaf-theoretic uniqueness theorem for the Schwarzian: up to O_X^* for fixed X, and up to C* when functorial for étale maps. On the following page it is continued to schemes over Z with Hasse derivatives, where the Schwarzian is unique up to sign ±1 after normalising by 1/12. The Z/±1 refinement (next page) seems the least standard part.
missed.quote: Si, au lieu de prendre X fixe, on prend X variable, avec morphismes étales entre les X, on a même résultat, et l'indétermination sera G'=cG  c∈C*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Relevant to projective structures and opers in positive and mixed characteristic (Mochizuki's indigenous bundles, dormant opers, Wakabayashi). An axiomatic characterisation of the integral (Hasse–Schmidt) Schwarzian over Z, unique up to sign, is not commonly stated in that literature.

missed.claim: The conjectured structure of the denominator (Q = f'^p g'^q for coprime P, Q) and the full proof of uniqueness are left as 'on doit pouvoir montrer'.
missed.quote: On doit pouvoir montrer que, si on prend P, Q premiers entre eux, on a pour n convenable Q=f'^p g'^q
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor; it is a routine statement in differential invariant theory, but a written proof in the arithmetic (Hasse derivative) setting would be needed for the Z-version.

deep.surprise_reason: The Schwarzian's cocycle and uniqueness properties and the torsor of projective structures are classical. What is distinctive is Grothendieck's functorial, sheaf-on-the-étale-site formulation with explicit tracking of the indeterminacy (O_X^* → C* → ±1 over Z, the last step on the next page). This is an unpublished but natural detail, not a major new result.
